chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Al-Hukrah (monopolizing a commodity) is when you buy food that is not available elsewhere in the city, so you hoard it; but if food is available in the city or other food is sold, there is no harm in seeking a premium for your goods."
He said: And I asked him about oil. He said: "If it is with others (i.e., available in the market), there is no harm in holding onto it."

key_terms.إِمْسَاكٌ: Holding onto goods (withholding from immediate sale)
key_terms.الْحُكْرَةُ: Monopoly or hoarding of goods to control price or availability

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on monopolizing food and hoarding goods in the market?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the concept of *hukrah* by distinguishing between absolute scarcity, where withholding is permissible, and market saturation, where hoarding to extract excessive premiums is discouraged. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preventing artificial price manipulation to protect public welfare (*maslaha*) while allowing legitimate profit in times of genuine shortage.
